findings.message: Bare `except:` with `pass` swallows every exception from charge() (including GatewayError and unexpected errors) instead of converting it to PaymentError; payment failures are silently hidden and callers cannot distinguish success from failure.
findings.suggestion: Catch the specific gateway exception (e.g. except GatewayError as exc) and re-raise PaymentError(f"charge failed for order {order.id}: {exc}") from exc; do not use a bare except/pass.

findings.message: If charge() raises before assigning result, the exception is swallowed and `return result` executes with an unbound local, raising UnboundLocalError (or returning a stale/undefined value) instead of the intended PaymentError.
findings.suggestion: Initialize result or re-raise inside the except block so control never reaches `return result` after a failed charge; e.g. raise PaymentError from exc in the handler and only return on success.
